source_caption:
Rounders — Risk, Loyalty & One Last Game

Rounders (1998) follows Mike McDermott, a talented poker player who gives up high-stakes gambling after losing a major game. Determined to build a more stable life, Mike focuses on law school and tries to leave the underground poker world behind.

But everything changes when his old friend Worm is released from prison. Worm's return brings Mike back into the dangerous world of underground poker, where huge amounts of money can be won or lost in a single hand.

As Mike gets pulled deeper into the game, he finds himself caught between his future, his friendship with Worm, and the debts that continue to follow them. Every decision becomes a gamble, and walking away becomes harder than ever.

The film explores themes of friendship, loyalty, ambition, temptation, risk, and redemption. It shows how difficult it can be to leave behind something you're naturally talented at, especially when the pressure to return is always there.

What makes Rounders compelling is the psychological battle behind every poker table. The biggest advantage isn't always the cards—it's knowing when to take a risk and when to walk away.

💬 Sometimes the biggest gamble isn't the hand you're playing—it's the choice to go all in.

source_details.synopsis: Rounders is a 1998 American crime drama film about the underground world of high-stakes poker, directed by John Dahl and starring Matt Damon and Edward Norton. The story follows two friends who need to win at high-stakes poker to quickly pay off a large debt. The term "rounder" refers to a person traveling around from city to city seeking high-stakes card games. Rounders premiered at the Venice Film Festival on September 4, 1998, and was theatrically released in the United States on September 11.
